requirements.evidence: The main flow is complete: sendInvite/cancelInvite (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:51-134`), accept/decline (`app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:28-88`), schema/model/factory/mail (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_061805_create_entity_invites_table.php`, `app/Models/EntityInvite.php:13-78`, `app/Mail/EntityInviteMail.php:13-37`), the members modals (`resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:92-155`), and lang/docs updates. Minor deviations remain: `PendingInvites::accept()` additionally requires a verified e-mail (`PendingInvites.php:107-110`) and `sendInvite()` deletes accepted invites as well as expired ones (`Members.php:91`).

conventions.evidence: Migrations/factories/docs mostly follow the project style, but public input properties use inline `validate([...])` instead of `#[Validate]`/`rules()` (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:25-34,57-59,164`), server-context properties are not `#[Locked]` (`Members.php:29,36`), domain writes are inline rather than in `app/Actions/*` (`Members.php:91-115`, `PendingInvites.php:52-57`), `PendingInvites` authorizes with `abort_unless` rather than a policy (`PendingInvites.php:100-113`), and the CHANGELOG entry is duplicated under the released `[0.0.0]` section (`CHANGELOG.md:40`).

security.evidence: The data-changing Members actions authorize server-side (`app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:53,123,138,158,183,201`), IDs are resolved from the entity-scoped relations (`Members.php:126,140,156,193`), input is validated (`Members.php:57-59,164`), and Blade uses `{{ }}` escaping. Remaining policy gaps are client-writable `selectedMembershipId`/`confirmingRemoval` (`Members.php:29,36`), unguarded local-state actions (`Members.php:148-151,188-191`), and invite-id enumeration through 403-vs-404 (`PendingInvites.php:102-110`); no exploitable path was found because the lookups are scoped.

tests.evidence: Extensive Pest coverage exists for model/schema/mail (`tests/Feature/Entity/EntityInviteTest.php`), accept/decline/authorization, switcher/onboarding, and the members flow, modals, rate limit, race, and tamper cases (`tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php:39-486`). Missing per-action unauthorized tests remain for `confirmRemoval`, `cancelRemoval`, `closeMember`, and a direct unauthorized `sendInvite` call (`MembersTest.php:224`).

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses the pending scope, `managerCount()`, the existing factory pattern, and livewire mail/render patterns; there is no speculative service layer. A little extra surface (`closeMember()`, `separator`) and large test helpers prevent a 5.

readability.evidence: Names and method boundaries are clear, and the Blade follows the existing Bulma/modal style. `Members::sendInvite()` is fairly long (`Members.php:51-119`) and the members view is 155 lines with two inline modals; owner checks also use the FQCN `\App\Models\UserRole::Owner` in Blade (`resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:103,122`).

scope.evidence: The production changes (invite flow, manager-only members page, modals, navbar/dashboard guards, docs) all serve the task. The only stray edit is the duplicate CHANGELOG entry under the released `[0.0.0]` section (`CHANGELOG.md:40`).

issues.explanation: Public input properties (`inviteEmail`, `inviteRole`, `memberRole`) have neither `#[Validate]` attributes nor a `rules()` method and are validated only by inline rule arrays in the actions, contrary to the project's mandatory Livewire validation pattern.

`selectedMembershipId` (a record ID) and `confirmingRemoval` (a flag) are client-writable and not `#[Locked]`; entity-scoped lookups limit the impact, but this violates the project's Livewire server-context rule.
`accept()` and `decline()` authorize with an inline `abort_unless` e-mail/verified check instead of a policy or gate, contrary to the project's authorization convention.

Domain writes such as invite creation, `EntityMembership::firstOrCreate()` (`PendingInvites.php:52-57`), and role updates are performed inline in Livewire components rather than through `app/Actions/*` use-case classes as the project requires.
`accept()` also requires a verified e-mail address, so an invitee whose e-mail matches but who has not verified gets 403; the task defines the acceptance gate as the e-mail match only.

`sendInvite()` deletes every invite for the address, including accepted invites, before inserting, although the task only permits replacing an expired invite; if the insert then fails, the previous row is also lost.

The employee-denial test only asserts that the component cannot mount; there are no unauthorized-call tests for `confirmRemoval`, `cancelRemoval`, `closeMember`, and no direct unauthorized test for `sendInvite`, although the project requires an unauthorized test for each action.
`closeMember()` and `cancelRemoval()` are public front-end actions but do not authorize; they only toggle local UI state, so the impact is low, but the Livewire policy asks every action to authorize.
The invite changelog entry is duplicated under the released `[0.0.0]` section instead of appearing only under `[Unreleased]`.
`findOrFail()` runs before the e-mail match, so an authenticated user can distinguish unknown invite IDs (404) from someone else's invite (403) and enumerate invite IDs; the impact is low.
The rate limit is incremented after the insert, so concurrent requests can all pass `tooManyAttempts()` before any `hit()` and exceed the 10/hour quota.
The owner check repeats the fully-qualified `\App\Models\UserRole::Owner` in Blade instead of using a view variable or helper, which is slightly harder to read than the surrounding code.

review.summary: The change implements the invite-only membership flow end to end, including the model/migration/factory, queued mail, pending-invite accept/decline, manager-only members page with the detail and removal modals, and a broad test suite. The main reasons for the overall score are project-policy deviations in the Livewire components (inline validation instead of `#[Validate]`, unlocked client-writable state, policy-free invite actions, domain writes outside Actions) plus a few extra or over-broad behaviors and missing per-action unauthorized tests. The feature is functionally close, but these should be fixed before merging.
